**Principle of Non‑Discrimination (Australian Framework for Generative AI in Schools)** The Non‑Discrimination principle is one of the core ethical guidelines that schools must follow when adopting generative AI (GAI) tools. Its purpose is to **prevent and counter any bias or unfair treatment that could arise from the use of these technologies**. In practical terms, the principle requires: | What it covers | Key actions/requirements | |----------------|--------------------------| | **Avoiding biased outputs** | • Select models that have been trained on diverse, representative data.
• Regularly audit outputs for patterns that could disadvantage any group (e.g., race, gender, disability, Indigenous status). | | **Transparency & explainability** | • Provide clear explanations of how a GAI tool makes decisions or generates content.
• Where full interpretability is impossible, offer a human‑readable “explainability” that highlights potential bias influences. | | **Equitable access** | • Ensure that tools are usable by all students, including those with disabilities and from diverse cultural or linguistic backgrounds.
• Offer alternative resources when a GAI solution is unsuitable for a particular learner. | | **Accountability & disclosure** | • Inform users (students, teachers, parents) when a GAI tool is being used and how it may affect them.
• Maintain logs or evidence that decisions were made fairly and without discriminatory intent. | | **Fair assessment** | • When GAI is used in marking or assessment, ensure the evaluation is unbiased, consistent, and reflects each student’s genuine ability.
• Validate that the tool does not systematically penalise any demographic group. | | **Cultural & intellectual‑property respect** | • Treat Indigenous knowledge and culturally sensitive content with respect, avoiding appropriation or misrepresentation by the AI. | **In short:** The Non‑Discrimination principle obliges schools to **monitor, test, and adjust** their use of generative AI so that it does not inadvertently reinforce stereotypes or exclusion. It is grounded in the broader goals of fairness, accessibility, and academic integrity that the Australian Framework promotes for all AI applications in education.
